A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 28-page versions of the same Multinex work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary Sections A-E can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-enhancement benchmarks, ExDark detection results, ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results from newly trained Multinex and Multinex-Nano models in Table 2.

M1.justification: The residual enhancement formulation, guidance stacks, fusion architecture, attention components and training losses are unchanged. Table 2 explicitly identifies the added models as retraining with the same architecture.

E1.justification: Section 4 removes the stated use of SDSD indoor/outdoor video data. LOL-v1, LOL-v2-real/synthetic, MEF, LIME, DICM, NPE and ExDark remain. Neither version presents SDSD outcomes, so this narrows stated coverage without removing demonstrated results.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments. Table 2 retains SNR-Net, LLFlow, CIDNet and ZeroDCE; the added dagger rows are retrained proposed models, not new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep the same splits, metrics, training settings and exclusion of GT-Mean processing. Table 2 explicitly states that the new models use the same training configuration and evaluation protocol. The deleted SDSD split descriptions accompany withdrawal of that dataset mention.

E4.justification: The prior, attention and loss ablations, descriptor analyses and challenging-image cases remain unchanged in Section 4.3 and supplementary Sections B, D and E. The new benchmark rows introduce no separate robustness or sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: The added retraining rows provide additional point estimates without introducing seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices otherwise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains all original scores and adds Multinex† and Multinex-Nano† results across four no-reference datasets. For example, Multinex† reports MEF NIQE/BRISQUE of 3.19/11.89 versus the retained 3.46/13.82, but NPE worsens to 3.82/13.09 from 3.71/12.52. Other numerical tables and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations remain unchanged, including the Retinex residual, guidance descriptors, fusion and loss equations, and supplementary PCA/ridge reconstruction and descriptor-importance definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-prior enhancement, lightweight and nano parameter efficiency, and benchmark performance. The new results do not introduce or redefine a core contribution.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including noise amplification, spectral distortions, clipped highlights and difficult lighting conditions. Supplementary Section E retains the same failure-case explanations; the new retraining results receive no additional interpretation.

D1.justification: The Table 2 caption newly identifies the dagger rows as retrained models using the conference version's architecture, training configuration and evaluation protocol. This adds limited provenance information; supplementary implementation details and project-page access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the SDSD reference, 'Seeing dynamic scene in the dark: A high-quality video dataset with mechatronic alignment,' alongside its dataset mention. The remaining cited works and research positioning are unchanged; subsequent citation-number shifts are mechanical.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the shortened dataset paragraph, the added retraining explanation in Table 2 and the updated arXiv header. The narrative, section organization and supplementary prose otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands from six to eight rows, adds dagger markers and an explanatory caption, and adjusts result highlighting. This causes local page reflow. All figures and the other table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Removing the SDSD claim without accompanying results improves scope consistency, and explicitly marked retraining rows add evidence. However, the new Table 2 BRISQUE means, 15.53 and 16.05, differ from the arithmetic averages of their displayed dataset scores, approximately 13.85 and 14.54, without explaining another aggregation. These useful additions and new reporting inconsistencies leave the net quality effect unclear.
